facts.raw_span: A 96-year-old man with benign prostatic disease and dementia presented after a collapse at home
normocytic anemia (hemoglobin 119 g/L)
D-dimer of 1095 ng/mL
normal troponin
normal C-reactive protein
neutrophilia (10.44 × 10^9/L)
a swollen right knee and thigh and extensive bruising
Lower limb ultrasound showed a patent venous system
a 45 mm popliteal artery aneurysm with an 11.4 × 5.2 cm medial leg hematoma
extensive bruising behind the right knee and posterior-medial thigh, a pulsatile mass extending into the mid-thigh, and a pulseless right foot without signs of acute ischemia
repeat hemoglobin was 77 g/L
Computed tomography angiography demonstrated a 4 × 5 cm saccular popliteal artery aneurysm with a large posterior thigh collection measuring approximately 23 × 3 cm
